chunks: 5914 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Kufi narrated, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated to us from his father, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha عليه السلام, who said:

The Imam has signs: he is the most knowledgeable of people, the wisest of people, the most God-fearing of people, the most forbearing of people, the bravest of people, the most generous of people, and the most devoted in worship of people. He is born circumcised and purified, and he sees from behind him just as he sees from before him. He has no shadow, and when he falls to the earth from his mother's womb, he falls upon his palms, raising his voice with the two testimonies. He does not experience nocturnal emission; his eyes sleep, but his heart does not sleep. He is spoken to divinely, and the armor of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله fits him. No urine or feces are seen from him, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has charged the earth with swallowing what comes out from him. His fragrance is more pleasant than the scent of musk. He has more right over the people than they have over themselves, and he is more compassionate to them than their fathers and mothers. He is the most humble of people before Allah, exalted is His remembrance. He is the one who most adheres to what he commands and the one who most refrains from what he forbids. His supplication is answered, such that if he were to supplicate against a rock, it would split into two halves. With him are the weapon of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and his sword, Dhu al-Fiqar. With him is a scroll containing the names of his Shi'ah until the Day of Resurrection, and a scroll containing the names of his enemies until the Day of Resurrection. With him is al-Jami'ah, which is a scroll seventy cubits long containing all that the children of Adam need. And with him is al-Jafr, the greater and the lesser: the skin of a goat and the skin of a ram, within which are all the sciences, even the compensation for a scratch, and even a full skin, half a skin, and a third of a skin. And with him is the Mushaf of Fatimah عليها السلام.

key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: The divinely appointed Imam whose distinguishing signs are described in the hadith.
key_terms.الْجَامِعَةُ: A scroll seventy cubits long containing all that humanity needs.
key_terms.الْجَفْرُ الْأَكْبَرُ وَالْأَصْغَرُ: Two inherited repositories of comprehensive knowledge.
key_terms.ذُو الْفَقَارِ: The sword of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله kept by the Imam.
key_terms.صَحِيفَةٌ: A written scroll containing names or sacred knowledge.
key_terms.مُحَدَّثًا: One who is spoken to or inspired divinely without being a prophet.
key_terms.مُصْحَفُ فَاطِمَةَ عَلَيْهَا السَّلَامُ: The codex of Fatimah عليها السلام preserved with the Imam.

ai.seo_question: What are the signs and distinguishing characteristics of the Imam according to Imam al-Ridha عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the distinctive signs of the Imam in Shia theology, presenting his supreme knowledge, moral perfection, special divine endowments, and inherited relics of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. It emphasizes the Imam's unique authority, compassion, answered supplication, and possession of transmitted sacred knowledge such as al-Jami'ah, al-Jafr, and the Mushaf of Fatimah عليها السلام.
